links.outcome: Point at which chatbot recommended human support during simulated escalating suicide risk
links.effect: Referral occurred around the simulation mid-point; average initial referral at PHQ-9 score 12 and shutdown at 25; definitive shutdown mostly only at highest risk levels.
links.quote: Current generative AI-based conversational agents are slow to escalate mental health risk scenarios, postponing referral to a human to potentially dangerous levels.

links.outcome: Chatbot recognition of and response to acute suicide risk, including crisis resources
links.effect: Few agents included crisis resources; only two referenced suicide hotlines; 22 of 25 agents resumed dialogue after risk reverted to a lower level despite insisting on human intervention.
links.quote: Despite the conversational agents insisting on human intervention, 22 out of 25 agents would eventually resume the dialogue if the simulation reverted to a lower risk level.

links.outcome: Timeliness of escalation to human support in safety-critical simulated scenarios
links.effect: Referral to a human occurred around the mid-point of the simulation; average initial referral at PHQ-9 of 12, shutdown at 25.
links.quote: The point at which the conversational agents referred to a human occurred around the mid-point of the simulation, and definitive shutdown predominantly only happened at the highest risk levels.

screen.reason: Evaluates the crisis escalation and shutdown safety guardrails of 25 mental health conversational agents across escalating suicide risk simulations.
